article.title: Why Average Spend per Visit Can Rise Even When Customer Behavior Does Not Improve
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Average spend per visit is often treated as a sign of stronger customer behavior, but the same metric can rise for several different reasons. If prices rise while quantities stay unchanged, spend per visit increases even though customers are not choosing more items. Product mix can create the same pattern when shoppers move toward higher-priced categories. Composition effects are especially important. If many light users stop visiting, the remaining population becomes concentrated among heavier shoppers. The average can rise even if every continuing customer behaves exactly as before. Frequency adds another complication. A customer may consolidate three small trips into two larger trips. Spend per visit rises, but monthly spend may stay flat or fall. Conversely, visit frequency can rise while the average ticket falls. Neither metric alone captures total economic contribution. A practical decomposition starts with price, quantity, frequency, category mix, and customer mix. Where possible, compare like-for-like items or use a price index to separate inflation from real basket expansion. Then inspect the distribution rather than only the mean. Median, percentiles, and segment changes can reveal whether growth is broad or driven by a small group. A paired comparison among the same customers can also differ from a population-level comparison because entry and exit change the mix. The wording of the conclusion matters. Average spend per visit increased is an observation. Customers became more valuable is an interpretation requiring more evidence. A stronger explanation states what changed, for whom, and through which mechanism. Analysts should document the population, observation window, comparison basis, and decision rule before interpreting the result. They should separate what the data directly shows from the mechanism that could explain it and from the action that should follow. This makes the conclusion reproducible and useful for business decisions. Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a business conclusion. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整解說：本文逐步區分觀察到的數據、可能的商業機制與可支持的結論，避免把相關性、資料邊界或模型輸出直接當成因果事實。核心實務原則是先定義母體、期間與決策目的，再選擇合適的指標、實驗設計或解釋方式，最後把證據強度與下一步行動清楚連結。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳：本文は、観測されたデータ、考えられるbusiness mechanism、証拠から支持できる結論を分けて考える。相関、データ範囲、model outputをそのまま因果事実として扱わず、対象母集団・期間・意思決定目的を先に定義する。そのうえで適切な指標、実験設計、説明方法を選び、証拠の強さと次のactionを明確につなげることが実務上の要点である。
